clara: Noticed a confusing UX during the intro workshop: Go generator iterator doesn't unwind reliably on cancel when auth retries + slow consumer coincide. Pasting repro + proposed ergonomics.

clara: Repro (minimal):
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
iter, _ := client.Generator(ctx, req) // pull iterator
_ = iter.Next() // read one piece
cancel() // parent cancelled, expect quick teardown
// sometimes iter.Next()/Close hang and goroutines remain
```

devlin: thanks. Is this only Iter or also the streaming callback API?

clara: Both hit it in workshop. Iter tends to hang in handshake/auth goroutines; Stream blocks on internal chan send when consumer is slow. Common theme: some goroutines don't select on the caller ctx.Done().

yuri: sounds like two roots we've seen: (A) channel send without ctx select -> backpressure deadlock; (B) auth refresher/retry using a derived ctx that isn't cancelled with parent.

devlin: immediate fixes: 1) ensure all spawned goroutines use the passed root ctx; 2) make every internal channel send use `select { case ch <- v: case <-ctx.Done(): return }`. That makes cancel deterministic.

clara: ergonomics proposals for API parity + onboarding:
- Add `iter.CloseWithTimeout(ctx, dur)` and `iter.ForceClose()` (ForceClose = immediate, may drop in-flight tokens).
- Expose `GeneratorOption{BackpressurePolicy: Block | BufferWithTimeout | DropOldest}` so demos can avoid blocking by default.
- Update quickstart with a snippet, e.g.:
```go
iter, _ := client.Generator(ctx, req)
defer func(){ _ = iter.CloseWithTimeout(context.Background(), 100*time.Millisecond) }()
for tok, ok := iter.Next(); ok; tok, ok = iter.Next() { /* handle */ }
```

yuri: parity note: Python has `aclose()` and Node has `.return()`; mapping those to `Close()` and `ForceClose()` in Go helps cross-language docs. Add a small table in DX docs.

devlin: implementation plan: short-term patch to thread ctx through auth refresher + select on sends; medium-term RFC to add CloseWithTimeout/ForceClose + BackpressurePolicy. Tests: add a flaky-tolerant integration that simulates slow consumer and asserts no goroutine leak within 200-300ms across go1.20-1.22.

clara: also add an onboarding note: "If you see generator hang during workshop, set BackpressurePolicy=BufferWithTimeout or call ForceClose in teardown." Will add to instructor checklist.

yuri: small UX nit: document ForceClose semantics loudly (may lose tokens, server-side partial state), and make ForceClose opt-in.

devlin: I'll open the GH issue with tiny repro + goroutine dump and assign the auth refresher patch to myself. yuri, can you draft the SDK RFC for API ergonomics?

yuri: yep will do. I'll include example mappings to Python/Node, snippet for CloseWithTimeout, and proposed BackpressurePolicy enum.

devex-bot: Issue created: DEX-6410 "go generator cancel teardown + backpressure ergonomics" (assignee: devlin) :white_check_mark:

clara: thanks team  added a short note to the quickstart so new users won't be blocked during workshops. :thumbsup:
